answer: In a Wesolowski-style VDF, each identity must complete a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings before it can produce a verifiable proof. The dependency between squarings prevents a GPU from shortening the elapsed time for one chain; running many cloned identities requires many chains and incurs corresponding compute and waiting costs. This creates a physical bottleneck per identity, not an absolute ban on parallel hardware—like copper winding, nectar ripening, or violet pigments, elapsed time cannot simply be wished away.
